Chapter 2: Who Doesn't Have a Childhood Sweetheart

After the second semester of their sophomore year, perhaps because they had grown up, the relationship between the two had eased up quite a bit. Now, in the blink of an eye, they were already in their senior year, but still somewhat at odds.

"Are you crazy, Jiang Nian!" The girl stood with her hands on her hips, glaring at him with puffed cheeks. "Why are you knocking on the door in broad daylight? I'm going to tell Auntie Li and have her give you a beating!"

Jiang Nian stared at Xu Qianqian, or to be precise, at the pale blue, semi-transparent panel in front of him.

As expected, only he could see it.

[Re-established contact with estranged childhood friend and fiancée, Xu Qianqian. Reward: 300 RMB (Completed).]

Whoa, has it arrived?

Xu Qianqian furiously cursed Jiang Nian out, then suddenly noticed that he seemed to be staring at her in a daze. The hairs on her arms stood up, and she took a step back, covering her well-endowed chest.

"W-why are you looking at me like that?"

Then, she saw Jiang Nian, as if he hadn't heard her, pull his phone out of his pocket and glance at it. Immediately overjoyed, he yelled out, "Yeehaw!" and ran off.

Watching Jiang Nian's back as he returned to the apartment opposite hers, Xu Qianqian couldn't help but purse her lips.

"Weirdo."

In the living room.

Jiang Nian hugged his phone, looking at it again and again, overjoyed.

Three hundred yuan had really appeared in his account out of thin air. The balance had changed from 305.23 to 605.23, and the transaction note said "Payment for Game Experience Officer."

At that moment, the panel reappeared. [At thirty-eight, you are in dire financial straits. Unemployed and divorced, you have lost almost all your assets and can only rely on your parents for support.

Mission: Urgent Need.

Using your first reward, pay off the overdue water, electricity, and gas bills for your rented apartment. Reward: 500 RMB.]

He figured this was probably a tutorial mission and opened the app to pay the bills. He didn't have a rented apartment, so paying his own family's gas, water, and electricity bills should count as completing the mission, right?

At the same time, he felt a bit wistful. Was his future self really that pathetic?

Buzz! Five hundred yuan arrived.

So far, the system's missions had been relatively easy. Jiang Nian checked his bank account balance. After paying more than 170 yuan in bills, his total balance was 935.45.

He was a practical person, and after the five hundred arrived, he gradually calmed down.

Two sums of five hundred were just a drop in the bucket; as long as it wasn't more than five thousand in a day, no one would bat an eye. But if it exceeded that amount in the future, it would be a lot of trouble.

Not only could his bank card be frozen, but large transfers might even trigger an investigation.

The sender was listed as Tianguang Games Co., Ltd. Jiang Nian looked it up and found that not only did this company exist, but it was also publicly listed, and their "Game Experience Officer" position had only one employee.

Of course, Jiang Nian wasn't foolish enough to believe this "placeholder job" was real, not to mention that current technology was nowhere near capable of creating a personal panel like this.

Besides, he wasn't some chief experience officer; it was purely the system patching up a bug in reality.

In other words, the source was reasonable and legitimate.

Awesome.

Just as he finished his search, the system panel appeared again. Another tutorial mission had arrived.

[By the time you wish to be filial, your parents are no longer there. At thirty-eight, you realize your parents have grown old. Looking back on a life half-lived, you resolutely embark on the journey home, feeling a sense of apprehension as you draw near.

Mission: Cook a lavish dinner for your parents.

Reward: 800 RMB.]

Looking at the mission requirement, Jiang Nian couldn't help but stroke his chin.

It was currently afternoon, so he had time to prepare dinner. Otherwise, he would have to wait until tomorrow. The school was on break for its anniversary celebration for the next two days, but he had to return for evening self-study tomorrow night. Cooking wasn't a problem; almost no one in the Jiang family couldn't cook.

When his grandfather was young, he had even worked as a chef in a Yangcheng restaurant. His father's and uncle's generation could all cook a few dishes. It was just that their results were less than satisfactory. When it came to his own dad…

In his grandfather's words, it was like putting scallions in a pig's snout.

Jiang Nian was an exception. His grades were average, but he had carved out his own path and had a bit of a talent for cooking. He didn't find the pastry and wok skills that others found difficult to be challenging at all.

Every summer vacation, he would religiously hole up at his grandfather's house, eating good food on one hand, while intermittently learning several signature dishes on the other. His cooking also tasted pretty decent.

Since it had to be lavish, the ingredients naturally had to be the freshest.

In the afternoon, Jiang Nian made a trip to the wet market, only to return disappointed. He had forgotten that there were hardly any fresh vegetables in the afternoon. A group of middle-aged vendors, seeing how young he was, even tried to pass off subpar produce as high-quality goods, raising the price before "discounting" it.

Sure enough, every merchant is a cheat, the bastards. There's a reason young people prefer supermarkets; these people at the wet market judge customers by their appearance. They deserve to go out of business.

By the time he had all the ingredients ready, it was already four o'clock when he got home.

On the quartz countertop in the kitchen lay a deboned and chopped Yangshan chicken. It was a famous specialty chicken from Guangdong, costing over thirty yuan per jin, with the price inflated to forty yuan per jin in Zhennan.

The meat was crisp, springy, and flavorful without being greasy. It was indeed worth the price.

He planned to make steamed chicken in lotus leaf. This chicken was expensive and had firm, tender meat, so it should definitely count as "lavish," right?

He would be more casual with the other dishes, planning to make a plate of stir-fried seasonal vegetables, a plate of stir-fried beef with peppers, smashed cucumber salad, fried peanuts, and a pot of pork rib soup to go with it.

The cost instantly skyrocketed. Just the ingredients for this one meal cost nearly four hundred yuan.

Normally, these dishes would be far too much for a family of three. But Jiang Nian considered Xu Qianqian next door. In a sense, the two of them really were childhood friends.

Xu Qianqian came from a single-parent family. Her mom had passed away a few years ago.

Her dad, Director Xu, was a renowned andrologist at the county hospital, having both castrated testicles and cured impotence. He always wore a pair of rimless glasses and greeted everyone with a gentle smile.

He had never quite moved on after his wife's death and spent all his time numbing himself with work.

Over the past few years, when the Jiang family faced difficulties, Old Xu had helped them out privately quite a bit. The two families were very close.

So even though his parents had been busy working to pay off debts these past few years, whenever they had good food at home, they would definitely call Xu Qianqian over. Even when cutting a melon, they had to give her the sweetest piece.

Jiang Nian was already used to it and had subconsciously included Old Xu and Xu Qianqian's portions in his calculations. It would be just enough for five people—lavish, but not wasteful when averaged out.

In the afternoon, Li Hongmei had just gotten off work. She hastily tied on an apron and rushed to the kitchen.

"Dinner will be ready soon. Go read a book, don't just play on your phone. You're almost a senior. Let me tell you, the college entrance exam is like a thousand soldiers crossing a single-log bridge."

Jiang Nian was lying on the sofa, a popsicle in his mouth as he played on his phone, not even lifting his head.

"Okay, got it, Mom."

"You child..." Li Hongmei wiped her hands on her apron. The moment she entered the kitchen, she froze, staring at the dishes being kept warm. She turned her head and glanced at Jiang Nian.

"Who cooked this?"

"I did. How is it?"

Hearing this, the expression on Li Hongmei's face instantly became complicated. It wasn't that she doubted Jiang Nian's cooking skills; the old man doted on his grandson and wished he could teach his precious grandkid all the skills he had acquired in his lifetime.

"Where did you get the money? This meal... Yangshan chicken, beef, it must have cost several hundred, right?"

"Ah, didn't I earn that money from playing games?" Jiang Nian touched his face, feeling a bit guilty. He held his breath and stared motionlessly at his mom, Li Hongmei.

Li Hongmei frowned, and the atmosphere in the kitchen instantly tensed.

(End of Chapter)
